recommendation:
  workflow:
    W-B: Varun receiving/invoice evidence → reviewed discrepancy → tracked resolution
  reason:
    Strongest overlap with demonstrated restaurant pack, PostgreSQL persistence, exact arithmetic, owner rules, replay and mixed-file intake; exercises current known failures without adding legal matter/date architecture.
  scope:
    One outlet, one receiving/invoice workflow, manager-confirmed quantities/identities and evidence-reviewed closure. GoFathom owns exception history only after explicit cutover; existing stock/accounting records remain authoritative.
  example:
    Invoice ₹2,240 versus accepted received value ₹2,137.60 → ₹102.40 unreconciled, subject to confirmed matching quantities/unit price and complete relevant evidence. This is a discrepancy, not automatically payable/refundable or proof of theft.
  not_first:
    Automatic payment, purchase or external inventory posting

    Inferring missing invoice/receipt values

    Ramya legal deadline or client-disclosure automation

    Native phone/desktop capture and agent-to-agent chat
  alternative:
    If restaurant source access or reviewer availability fails S0, compare Ramya read-only court-email triage or Varun issue closure using actual access and observed demand. Do not switch solely because another connector seems easy.
  sequence:
    Finish Varun review loop; validate restaurant issue closure or Ramya matter intake next according to evidence. General core remains reusable.
sprints:
  id:
    S0
  timebox:
    2 working days
  owner:
    Engineering lead + QA/reviewer
  goal:
    Pin the actual baseline on the other Mac
  tasks:
    Read actual AGENTS.md and current sprint/review records; resolve latest uncommitted changes and commit/hash manifest.

    Map all 27 H/C rows to code or explicit absence; identify app, CLI and worker paths.

    Re-run offline focused tests and inspect current whole-suite failures/security alerts; do not label historical blockers fixed without evidence.

    Recover exact fixture/output/usage receipts; no new paid tests or live-source activation required.
  exit:
    Reproducible test command and exact commit/snapshot recorded.

    Every row has code evidence or an explicit limitation; existing blockers triaged and owners assigned.
  dependencies:
    Access on the implementation Mac or a sanitized source/test bundle.

  id:
    S1
  timebox:
    5 working days
  owner:
    Domain/backend engineer + Varun or named operations reviewer
  goal:
    Repair the intake and record boundaries
  tasks:
    Separate event time, document time, instruction effective time and approval time; preserve unknowns.

    Normalize unambiguous currency/quantity formatting and duplicate source refs while retaining originals; ambiguous locale/unit stays unresolved.

    Block invoice-line admission until parent dependency is valid; handle rejection and reinstatement without orphan effects.

    Resolve table-to-outlet/item/unit mappings from evidence, never guessed names.

    Keep operational rule proposals even when effective time needs clarification; separate one-entry acceptance from standing policy.
  exit:
    Saved RUN03 defects reproduced before repairs; protected regressions and contrasting unseen variants pass offline.

    Unknown time never fabricated; valid ₹1,152 and equivalent supported forms retained; no cross-outlet or parentless acceptance.
  dependencies:
    S0 baseline

  id:
    S2
  timebox:
    5 working days
  owner:
    Full-stack engineer + QA
  goal:
    Deliver one review-to-resolution loop through the actual app
  tasks:
    Assemble critical amounts/status/actions from accepted current record versions plus deterministic calculations.

    Expose evidence, current state and calculations through small scoped read interfaces; full exploratory agent search remains optional.

    Connect fresh intake, review, corrections, exception ownership and outcome evidence to the real Today/Chat/Manage path.

    Implement only missing workflow pieces after the audit; preserve evidence-backed unknown and disputed states.

    Exercise change invalidation, access revocation, retries and restart through APIs/UI, not test-runner-only shortcuts.
  exit:
    Fresh permitted files → pending records → owner review → discrepancy → assigned follow-up → evidence-reviewed closure works through app.

    No repeated approval request for accepted record; source correction stales affected answer/check; closure needs evidence and reviewer.
  dependencies:
    S1 correct records

  id:
    S3
  timebox:
    5 working days, paid calls separately bounded
  owner:
    QA/evaluation engineer + domain reviewer
  goal:
    Prove generalization and measure cost before adding infrastructure
  tasks:
    Freeze 24 independent episode specifications: ordinary deliveries, supported formatting, corrections/time, identity/scope, missing/contradictory evidence, instruction/parent dependency cases. Reserve 12 as hidden holdout; repeated questions are not independent episodes.

    Run whole fresh-source path including required media; audit omissions as well as emitted candidates.

    Compare raw-context and simple-summary controls against structured path using same sources, model, tasks and adjudication; count ingestion, model, reviewer and support cost.

    Record exact mismatch, false alerts, unresolved cases, action outcomes, p50/p95 timings and known/unknown costs.

    After correctness is stable, measure changed-evidence processing and selective retrieval at 1x/10x/100x fixture histories; preserve context/correction equivalence.
  exit:
    All declared must-not-fail invariants pass; any unsupported critical amount/status/action, scope leak or duplicate effect blocks expansion.

    Missing inputs produce justified unknowns; clear in-scope facts cannot earn a pass by abstaining.

    Results and limitations reported with counts and uncertainty; no promised efficiency gain.
  dependencies:
    S2 app path; explicit finite paid-call budget if real models used

  id:
    S4
  timebox:
    10 business days observation, extend if event coverage insufficient
  owner:
    Pilot owner + engineering/support owner + Varun/designated reviewer
  goal:
    Bounded one-outlet shadow pilot
  tasks:
    Verify selected source identity, actual provider-visible scope, session health, credentials and media availability.

    Use one restaurant receiving stream and existing source-of-truth records; retain manual process as authority.

    Reconcile independent receiving/invoice register against intake daily; expose missing intervals and review backlog.

    Human approves record acceptance and closure; supplier contact, purchasing, payments and external ledger writes stay manual.

    Record C16 terms, C17 field bindings and C18 reliance scope, retention/deletion and escalation/fallback; price offer separate from claimed savings.
  exit:
    Owner can trace each pilot discrepancy to source and disposition; no silently lost eligible cases in the audited sample.

    Review/support time, unresolved amounts and closure time compared with baseline; owner explicitly accepts next scope.

    No automatic expansion based solely on calendar completion or an accuracy average.
  dependencies:
    S3 gates, release blockers closed for scope, customer consent and reliable source access
estimate:
  total:
    About 5–6 calendar weeks to a bounded shadow-pilot decision, not production launch
  assumptions:
    Experienced engineer available full time, part-time independent QA and prompt domain review; current core reusable; no major access/security blockers. S0 must revise estimates using real source.
  no_new_framework:
    Retain current TypeScript/PostgreSQL/worker foundation until source audit demonstrates a concrete gap; do not migrate to an agent framework to treat semantic boundary defects.
metrics:
  Source observation coverage with denominator provenance and unknown gaps

  Eligible-case recall and false-positive exceptions, split by consequence and modality

  Wrong outlet/identity/unit/date/status and unsupported amount claims

  Review minutes per eligible episode including false alarms, unresolved cases and corrections

  End-to-end acknowledged and evidence-closed exceptions; no completion credit for message send

  Ingest-to-review freshness and p50/p95 answer latency on stated workload

  Provider/infrastructure/support cost and customer labor separately; cost per verified resolution

  Incremental processing/retrieval resources versus history size at equal correctness
complexity:
  status:
    Analytical expectation only; not measured product behavior
  current:
    Chat reports large-history context (~37k input tokens per answer in one experiment) and excessive reprocessing; source complexity cannot be established here.
  proposed:
    For history bytes H and changed bytes Δ plus required context C, extraction should process Δ+C rather than H where dependencies allow. Corrections may require a larger affected dependency closure. Indexed lookup cost depends on query/index/selectivity; exact retrieval remains bounded by returned evidence bytes. Storage grows with source/derivative/revision retention; do not claim constant memory or guaranteed speedup.
boundary:
  Foundation 1.0 and 1.1 remain preserved. This edition publishes an evidence audit and proposed sprint plan, not product changes. Current runtime source, tests and receipts remain on another MacBook.
other_mac_audit_prompt:
  Audit our actual restaurant-assistant implementation on this MacBook against GoFathom architecture 1.1. Treat this as a source-code and execution-evidence audit, not another architecture discussion.

1. Architecture: https://vamsi-paltribe.github.io/supabiz-system-atlas/gofathom-1.1/llms-full.txt
2. Structured blueprint: https://vamsi-paltribe.github.io/supabiz-system-atlas/gofathom-1.1/blueprint.json

The 1.2 audit was based on our shared implementation conversation through 16 October 2026. Its author could not inspect this MacBook's runtime. Reconcile it with the current source and later work. Do not assume either that all reported features work or that unverified features are absent. Ignore the older ai-agent-for-WA repository; it is not this implementation.

Work in the existing restaurant-assistant checkout. Read its actual AGENTS.md, SPRINT-04.md, review rules and latest experiment/verification records. Preserve local changes. Identify the current branch, commit and dirty state; hash the relevant source and fixtures if the audited snapshot differs from HEAD. Check for active runners before starting anything; do not duplicate a running test or review.

Audit all nine harness responsibilities H01-H09 and all 18 contracts C01-C18. For each, record:
- Actual code path and symbol, or explicit absence.
- API, app-chat, CLI and worker entrypoints, including divergent paths.
- What exists, what is partial, what fails, and what remains unknown.
- Exact test IDs, commands, execution results and retained evidence.
- Revision/snapshot tested and limitations of the test.
- Status: absent, partial, present-untested, tested-at-commit, or blocked by unavailable evidence. A module name or test-count total is not a passing implementation.

Verify the complete path using synthetic inputs and provider stubs first:
new chats/files -> candidate records -> owner accept/reject/correct -> accepted current state -> deterministic calculation -> actual app-chat answer -> tracked discrepancy -> evidence-reviewed closure.
Distinguish real UI/API integration from a backend experiment runner. Reuse the existing TypeScript, PostgreSQL, worker, storage, calculation and review components.

Inspect and reproduce these known failure classes before recommending fixes:
1. The 20 kg operational rule being dropped because effective time was unclear.
2. The valid Rs 1,152 invoice rejected for comma formatting or repeated evidence references.
3. Invoice lines continuing to contribute after rejection of their parent.
4. An answer asking approval for an already accepted receipt.
5. Missing deterministic calculations while the model is told not to calculate.
6. Wrong-outlet forwards, same-name people, ambiguous units and table-to-item mappings.
7. Unknown event time, late corrections and distinct document/effective/approval dates.
8. Gross invoice versus net payable versus reported/confirmed payment and supporting citations.
Use contrasting cases; retain original failures. Identify whether the most recent proposed boundary repairs have actually been implemented since the shared-chat snapshot.

Inspect the 1.1 controls explicitly: source coverage versus processing accounting, exclusions and zero-candidate assessments, field-authority/version binding, parser isolation, grant/revocation checks, instruction overrides/expiry, current-state invalidation, and effect intent/receipt/transmit-marker cancellation. Provider-call accounting does not prove business-action reconciliation. Audit task acknowledgement and closure separately from message sending. Identify which controls are required before the first pilot and which are deliberately deferred.

Inspect test scripts before running them. Run appropriate offline checks in the project's existing isolated test environment. Preserve source fixtures and customer state. Report current failures, including previously recorded full-suite, formatting and security blockers. Do not infer they are fixed from a focused pass. Do not print secrets or environment values. No paid calls, live-source activation, deployment, new schedules, dependency upgrades or product-code changes are requested by this audit. If any required check is unsafe or unavailable, record the concrete limit and continue independent audit work.

Keep reviewer evidence exact and bounded. Follow applicable repository review requirements; a reviewer must see the actual relevant source and competing explanations. Do not replace execution evidence with reviewer agreement or claim a test passed because an earlier chat said so.

Evaluate this proposed first workflow: one Varun outlet, receiving/invoice evidence -> manager-reviewed discrepancy -> assigned follow-up -> evidence-reviewed resolution. Existing stock/accounting systems remain authoritative; no automatic purchasing, payment, supplier send or external ledger write. Challenge this choice if current code, access or demand supports a better one. Explain the alternative using evidence, not preference for a framework.

Produce a local dated audit folder containing:
1. AUDIT-REPORT.md: concise verdict, reusable code, ranked gaps/defects and unresolved questions.
2. audit-matrix.json: all 27 H/C rows with paths, revision, status and test evidence.
3. evidence-manifest.json: audited file hashes and exact test commands/results.
4. sprint-plan.md: revised small sprints, dependencies, owners/roles, estimates and measurable exit gates, grounded in inspected code.
5. handoff-summary.txt: what changed from the 1.2 evidence audit, what is now verified and what still blocks a pilot.

Keep raw receipts private. If preparing a handoff bundle, include only necessary source, migrations, synthetic fixtures and sanitized reports; exclude credentials, .env files, session stores, customer conversations, databases and node_modules. Do not publish or upload the bundle automatically.

Finish with an honest answer to: What works now? What is broken? What is missing? What can we reuse? Which exact next implementation task delivers the most useful verified progress? Do not declare the whole assistant complete or invent performance improvement percentages.
